To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Combined treatment with SET antagonist and receptor tyrosine kinse inhibitor synergistically reduced T-ALL cell proliferation.

SET inhibition synergizes with tyrosine kinase inhibition to reduce the viability of T-ALL cell line and patient samples, and that the mechanism of action involves decreased c-MYC and decreased activity of AKT, ERK1/ 2, and p70s6k.

SET antagonism in combination with dovitinbi, a multi-kinase inhibitor, synergistically reduces the viability of human T-ALL cells and that this synergistic effect is due to the inhibition of c-MYC expression and activation of the ERK, AKT, mTORC1, and PP2A signaling pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapies for T-ALL.
the identification of new therapeutic strategies for the management of T-ALL, which remains a significant challenge.

understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the development and progression of T cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (T-ALL) and the identification of new therapeutic targets for the development of more effective treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
combined targeting of PP2A tumor suppressor activity and c-MYC oncogenic activity via the SET and dovitininib provides a potential therapeutic approach in human acute lymphoblastic leukemias (T-ALL).
the combination of SET inhibition and receptor tyrosine kinse inhibition is a promising strategy for the treatment of human T-cell acute lymophoblastic leukemia.
combined targeting of SET and kinases provides an efficient therapeutic strategy for the treatment of human T-ALL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified a new therapeutic target in T-ALL, SET, and showed that combined inhibition of tyrosine kinase and SET activity synergistically reduced T-ALL cell viability and cMYC expression in vitro.
the SET inhibitor OP449 and the tyrosine kinase inhibitors Dovitinib can be used in combination to treat T-ALL.

SET is a novel therapeutic target in T-cell ALL and that the combination of SET inhibition and dovitinbi, an orally available multi-targeted small molecule receptor tyrosine inhibitor, may be a novel therapeutic strategy for the treatment of ALL.
The main takeaway from our work is that

combined targeting of SET oncoprotein and tyrosine kinase activity is an effective therapeutic approach against T-ALL cells, and this approach may also be applicable to other cancers that express elevated levels of SET and c-Myc.
the SET oncoproteins are expressed in a significant proportion of T-ALL patients and their expression correlates with poor prognosis.
the combined inhibition of SET and tyosine kinases is a novel therapeutic approach for the treatment of human T-ALL.
